battle.name: 烏邁耶征服西班牙
battle.theater: 安達盧斯與直布羅陀海峽
battle.brief: 七一一年春，倭馬亞將領塔里克·伊本·齊亞德率柏柏爾聯軍橫渡直布羅陀海峽，在耶貝爾·塔里克登陸；同年七月於瓜達萊特河畔擊潰西哥特王羅德里克的大軍，八月托勒多淪陷。遠征軍步兵以密集長矛線作戰，卡面這件埃及長矛正是這條武器譜系的源頭。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰方是西哥特托勒多王國與倭馬亞哈里發國的安達盧斯遠征軍。倭馬亞一方由北非伊弗里基亞總督穆薩·伊本·努薩爾節制，主力是北非柏柏爾諸部落的聯軍：先鋒由突尼斯出身的柏柏爾將領塔里克·伊本·齊亞德率領，統帶加納塔系（Ǧanāta）部眾，穆薩本人統馬斯穆達系（Masmūda）部眾，另有米克納薩等小部族隨行，其中混雜一部分由敘利亞調來的阿拉伯騎兵與輔兵。遠征軍編制沿用倭馬亞行省的軍團制：步兵按旗隊（firqa）編為數百人一隊，騎兵按百人隊編制，後勤完全依賴北非基地的船運補給，沒有長距離的輜重車隊。西哥特一方是七一〇年仍以托勒多為都的托勒多王國：國王羅德里克直接控制的王畿兵與南部各公爵的私兵鬆散拼成聯軍，兵種以持大橢圓盾的步兵與重騎兵為主，另有數量可觀的輕裝弓箭手；王國東部的加泰隆尼亞仍處在阿基泰利亞公國的半獨立狀態。真正決定戰局的第三方是塞塔伯爵朱利安：他控制直布羅陀海峽南岸的港口，選擇倒向遠征軍，替阿拉伯人提供了渡海所需的船隻與嚮導，也切斷了西哥特王國對海峽的警戒。
countriesEn: The opposing sides were the Visigothic kingdom of Toledo, the last western heir of Roman Hispania, and the Umayyad army of conquest in al-Andalus. On the Umayyad side the command lay with Musa ibn Nusayr, governor of Ifriqiya in North Africa, and the bulk of the force was a coalition of Berber tribes: the vanguard was led by the Berber commander Tariq ibn Ziyad, who brought the Zenata (Janata) peoples, while Musa led the Masmuda in person, with smaller groups such as the Miknasa alongside; among them were folded a body of Arab cavalry and auxiliaries drawn from Syria. The expedition followed the army organisation of the Umayyad provinces: infantry was grouped in banners of several hundred men, the firqa, cavalry in hundreds, and supply ran entirely by sea from the North African base, with no long land train behind the army. On the Visigothic side stood the kingdom of Toledo, which in 710 still had a king in Toledo: the royal levies of the crown and the private contingents of the southern duchies were loosely welded into a single field army, made up mainly of infantry with large oval shields and of heavy cavalry, with a substantial body of light archers; in the east the kingdom of Aquitaine was still half-independent under its own duke. The decisive third party was the count of Ceuta, Julian: he held the ports on the south shore of the strait, chose to side with the invaders, gave them the ships and the pilots they needed to cross, and cut the Visigothic watch on the narrows off at the root.
people: 關鍵人物有五位。塔里克·伊本·齊亞德是全軍的先鋒與最關鍵的指揮者：他原是穆薩在北非的釋奴與部眾首領，名字本意是「右翼」；七一一年春率軍橫渡海峽，未待主力即在耶貝爾·塔里克登陸，隨後以奇襲攻入安達盧斯，因為戰功被加封為加奈特（Ǧanāta）部落的統帥，海峽那座岩石山也從此以他命名。穆薩·伊本·努薩爾是伊弗里基亞總督，名義上是這場戰爭的統帥，實則更多在後方督運船隊與援兵：他率主力登陸後沿海岸北進，八月進入托勒多，同年冬天進入薩拉戈薩，此後更因戰利品分配與塔里克起了嫌隙。塞塔伯爵朱利安的選擇是整場戰爭的轉折點：西哥特方面的說法是他叛國，開啟了海峽；後世傳說則把他寫成受基督教迫害者、反而替異教徒開路，形象幾經改寫。西哥特國王羅德里克在瓜達萊特會戰中陣亡，結束了統治伊比利亞近三百年的西哥特王室；科爾多瓦主教奧勒留斯隨後成為莫薩拉布教會的保護人。第五位是預示後局的優素福·伊本·阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·菲赫里：他於七一八年被蘇萊曼任命為安達盧斯總督，平定貝都林人的騷亂，確立了倭馬亞對伊比利亞的長期統治。
peopleEn: Five figures stand at the centre of the war. Tariq ibn Ziyad was the vanguard and the decisive commander of the expedition: originally a freedman and client of Musa in North Africa, his name simply means 'right hand'; in the spring of 711 he crossed the strait ahead of the main body, landed at Jabal Tariq without waiting for the rest of the army, drove into al-Andalus by surprise, and was rewarded with the command of the Janata Berbers, after whom the rocky hill at the narrows has been named ever since. Musa ibn Nusayr, governor of Ifriqiya, was commander in name but spent more of his time behind, shipping up the fleet and the reinforcements: he came ashore with the main body, moved north along the coast, entered Toledo in August and reached Zaragoza in the winter of the same year, and afterwards fell out with Tariq over the division of the spoils. The choice made by the count of Ceuta, Julian, was the turning point of the whole war: Visigothic accounts call him a traitor who opened the strait, while later legend recast him as a man oppressed by Christianity who in fact opened the road to the unbelievers, and his figure was rewritten several times over. The Visigothic king Roderic fell at Guadalete, which ended a royal line that had ruled in Iberia for close to three centuries; Aurelius, bishop of Cordoba, then became the protector of the Mozarabic church. The fifth figure foretells what comes next: Yusuf ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri, appointed governor of al-Andalus by Sulayman in 718, put down the Berber disturbances and settled the long Umayyad hold on Iberia.
kits: 卡面這件綁在木杆上的銅矛頭長矛，正是遠征軍步兵的骨幹。埃及早王朝的長矛是這條技術路線的源頭：狹長的銅或青銅矛頭以銅箍或綁紮固定在木杆上，杆長超過兩公尺，雙手握於腰際，與左手的小圓盾配合；它的價值不在金屬，而在「線」——大量步兵排成密集縱隊，前排矛尖連成一道長矛牆，靠整列的縱深而不是單兵的力氣抵擋衝鋒。七一一年在安達盧斯作戰的柏柏爾步兵用的正是這類長矛與短標槍：矛頭已是鐵製，卻沿用同樣的握法與同樣的密集隊形。遠征軍步兵以小圓盾護住左臂，右手持矛，遇敵先拋標槍再挺矛衝鋒，靠速度與混戰取勝，不靠裝甲。阿拉伯騎兵配長矛與彎刀、披輕甲，衝鋒之後即回捲重整；柏柏爾騎兵更善長游走迂迴，把敵陣分割成碎塊。守方的西哥特步兵延續晚期羅馬的組合：橢圓大盾配長矛與標槍，盾緣互相咬合，正面極難突破；他們的長處是裝備與經驗，短處是各公爵私兵之間缺乏統一指揮，也沒有艦隊能在海峽攔截敵人。攻城手段以封鎖港口、斷絕糧道、逼降城邑為主，投石機與攻城塔在安達盧斯的記載要到數百年後才出現。
kitsEn: The bronze-headed spear lashed to a wooden shaft on the card is exactly the backbone of the expedition's infantry. The early dynastic Egyptian spear is the head of this technical line: a narrow copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft with a metal collar or binding, the shaft more than two metres long, gripped in both hands at the waist and used together with the small round shield on the left arm; its value lay not in the metal but in the line, for masses of infantry stood in dense columns and the front rank's points joined into a wall of spears, holding a charge by the depth of the formation rather than by the strength of any one man. The Berber infantry who fought in al-Andalus in 711 used precisely this class of weapon, a long thrusting spear and short javelins: the heads were already iron, but the grip and the dense formation were the same. The expedition's infantry covered the left arm with a small round shield, held the spear in the right hand, threw javelins before closing to push home, and won by speed and by the melee rather than by armour. Arab cavalry carried lances and sabres in light armour and wheeled back to reform after the charge; Berber horsemen were better at wide circuits and harrying, cutting the enemy formation into pieces. The Visigothic foot in the defended lines continued the late Roman combination of large oval shield, thrusting spear and javelin, with shield edges locked against one another and a front that was very hard to break; their strength lay in equipment and experience, their weakness in the absence of a unified command among the duchy levies and of any fleet able to contest the strait. Reduction of towns was achieved by sealing ports, cutting supply and forcing surrender; traction engines and siege towers do not enter the records of al-Andalus until centuries later.
tactics: 戰術層面是一次典型的輕裝奇襲遇上分節的守軍。遠征軍把渡海放在最要緊的第一位：北非的船匠在丹吉爾與塞塔造船，人力不足處以繃帶縫合木板（西班牙編年史有這樣的記載，細節或有誇張），登陸時步兵與馬匹分別上陸，馬匹多由游泳牽渡。塔里克沒有在塞塔正面登陸，而是選擇海峽北岸那片名叫耶貝爾·塔里克的岩岸，讓守軍以為敵人還在海上，隨即以步兵縱隊配合弓手掩護直取內陸。安達盧斯方面的反應是典型的西哥特式：羅德里克集結南部各公爵的部隊與王畿兵，排出以步兵居中、重騎兵兩翼的寬正面，試圖用一次正面衝鋒把來敵打散。戰局在瓜達萊特河畔崩壞：貝都林人騎兵不加掩護地反覆衝擊兩翼，把不聽統一號令的公爵私兵拉成碎片；羅德里克陣亡後中央縱隊失去指揮，潰兵互相踐踏，朱利安部下的據說在關鍵時刻撤出，兩翼先崩而中軍繼之瓦解。得勝後遠征軍沒有急著深入，反而停下來收編降軍、與托勒多的教會達成協議、把海峽兩岸的據點連成一片，並以快速分遣隊掃清殘餘抵抗：七一三年取托爾托薩與穆爾西亞，七一八年平定加泰隆尼亞與塞普蒂曼尼亞的殘餘據點，征服才告一段落。
tacticsEn: At the level of tactics this was a typical light-invasion surprise meeting a segmented defence. The expedition put the crossing first among all its concerns: shipwrights in Tangier and Ceuta built the fleet, and where timber was short the hulls were said to be planked and sewn together with cords, as the Spanish chronicles record, though the detail may be exaggerated; on landing, infantry and horses came ashore separately, the horses mostly being swum across on ropes. Tariq did not land in force against Ceuta but chose the rocky shore north of the strait called Jabal Tariq, so that the defenders would think the enemy was still at sea, and then drove inland with columns of infantry covered by archers. The Visigothic response was of the old Gothic type: Roderic gathered the contingents of the southern duchies with the royal levies, drew up a wide front with infantry in the centre and heavy cavalry on the wings, and tried to break the enemy with a single frontal charge. The battle broke apart on the banks of the Guadalete: Berber cavalry charged the flanks again and again without cover, pulling the dukes' private levies, which obeyed no common signal, into pieces; when Roderic fell the central column lost its commander, the fugitives trampled one another, and Julian's men are said to have withdrawn at the critical moment, the wings going first and the centre following. Having won, the expedition did not hurry inland: it paused to take in the surrendered, to come to terms with the church at Toledo, to string its strongholds together on both shores of the strait, and to clear the remaining resistance with fast flying columns, taking Tortosa and Murcia in 713 and finishing off the last strongholds in Catalonia and Septimania in 718.
data: 可核對的數字集中在幾處。時序上，遠征軍於七一一年春渡海，瓜達萊特會戰在同年七月，托勒多於八月十日落入遠征軍之手，薩拉戈薩同年秋攻克，七一三年托爾托薩與穆爾西亞淪陷，七一八年通常被視為安達盧斯征服的終點。地理上，直布羅陀海峽最窄處約十三至十四公里，耶貝爾·塔里克與斯帕泰爾角隔海相望；從登陸地到瓜達萊特戰場，沿海岸的道路約三百公里，因此從春天到七月有足夠時間完成籌備與推進。兵力方面，阿拉伯史料與後世編年史對遠征軍給出七千至一萬二千的數字，現代研究大致採信這個量級；西哥特方面的軍隊，十九世紀以前的阿拉伯文獻有誇大到數十萬的說法，現代史家多修正為數萬之數，瓜達萊特一役常估在四萬上下，其中公國私兵佔相當比重。此外兩點是硬數據：西哥特人自四一八年受羅馬冊封、定居阿基泰尼算起，到七一一年王室覆亡，存續接近三百年；以及戰後伊比利亞的城邑統計——托勒多、薩拉戈薩、托爾托薩、穆爾西亞等大城市在數年內相繼淪陷，說明遠征軍的縱深補給線短到可以只靠北非的船運維持。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers sit in a few places. On the chronology: the expedition crossed in the spring of 711, the battle of Guadalete came in July of the same year, Toledo fell into the invaders' hands on 10 August, Zaragoza was stormed in the autumn, Tortosa and Murcia were lost in 713, and 718 is conventionally treated as the end of the conquest of al-Andalus. On the geography: the strait of Gibraltar is about thirteen to fourteen kilometres wide at its narrowest, with Jabal Tariq facing Cape Spartel across the water; the road along the coast from the landing place to the field of Guadalete is some three hundred kilometres, so that the months from spring to July gave ample time for preparation and advance. On numbers of men, the Arabic sources and the later chronicles give the expedition between seven thousand and twelve thousand, and modern scholarship broadly accepts that order of magnitude; for the Visigothic host, pre-nineteenth-century Arabic texts inflate the figure to hundreds of thousands, while modern historians have revised it down to tens of thousands, the army at Guadalete commonly being put at around forty thousand, with a considerable share in the levies of the duchies. Two harder figures can be added: from the Roman settlement of the Visigoths in Aquitaine in 418 to the fall of the royal line in 711, the Visigothic state had lasted close to three centuries; and the count of towns in Iberia after the war, with Toledo, Zaragoza, Tortosa and Murcia falling within a few years of one another, shows that the expedition's line of communication was short enough to be kept alive by sea transport from North Africa alone.
cause: 這場戰爭的起因有遠因，也有直接導火線。遠因是倭馬亞帝國在阿卜杜勒·馬利克改革後形成的中央集權與持續對外擴張：瓦利德一世在位時，北非伊弗里基亞總督穆薩已多次試探直布羅陀一線，七一〇年的第一次渡海遠征便被西哥特人擋在「赫拉克勒斯之柱」外的塞塔與西班牙沿岸；七一一年再試，是因為海峽對岸的局勢出現了裂縫。直接導火線是西哥特王國內部的崩解：羅德里克在一場宮廷變亂中推翻前任國王瓦爾多瑪，逐出其黨羽並引發南部公爵與教會的普遍不滿，國王與朱利安伯爵的對立最終演成公開決裂。地理與技術上的機會同樣關鍵：西哥特人雖據有伊比利亞，卻沒有可以與北非抗衡的海軍，造船技術與航海經驗皆在敵手一側；而塞塔伯爵朱利安帶著港口與船隻投敵，等於把海峽這道門戶交了出去。加上北非柏柏爾部落長期以掠奪為業，又對安達盧斯的財富懷有覬覦，遠征一旦開打便難以中止：奪取戰利品的衝動與分贓不均，最終讓穆薩與塔里克兩族在安達盧斯互相猜忌。
causeEn: The war had both a distant cause and a proximate trigger. The distant cause was the centralisation and continuous outward expansion of the Umayyad caliphate after the reforms of Abd al-Malik: under al-Walid I the governor of Ifriqiya, Musa, had already probed the Gibraltar line several times, and the first crossing of 710 was thrown back by the Visigoths at Ceuta and along the Spanish coast beyond the Pillars of Hercules; the second attempt in 711 came because fissures had opened in the situation across the strait. The proximate trigger was the disintegration inside the Visigothic kingdom: Roderic had overturned his predecessor Valdmar in a palace coup, expelled the defeated faction, and provoked the general disaffection of the southern dukes and the church, and the quarrel between king and count Julian finally broke out in open rupture. The opportunities of geography and technique mattered just as much: the Visigoths held Iberia but had no navy that could match North Africa, and shipbuilding and seamanship lay on the enemy's side of the water; and the count of Ceuta went over with his ports and his ships, handing the gateway of the strait over with them. Add to that the fact that the North African Berber tribes had long lived on plunder and eyed the wealth of al-Andalus, and once the crossing had begun it was hard to stop: the drive for booty and the quarrelling over its division left the house of Musa and the house of Tariq suspicious of each other in al-Andalus.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果遠超伊比利亞。短期看，公元四一八年以來延續近三百年的西哥特王國在一年之內瓦解：國王陣亡、主都陷落，托勒多的主教與貴族接受改宗並保留教會與地產安排，莫薩拉布基督徒社群在安達盧斯延續了數個世紀，成為後來比利牛斯山以北基督教世界的橋樑。穆斯林安達盧斯自此在伊比利亞半島建立，前八十年由大馬士革的哈里發直接管轄，七五六年敘利亞的倭馬亞王子阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼一世渡海抵達科爾多瓦，建立獨立的埃米爾國，並以科爾多瓦為都，此後三個世紀是安達盧斯的黃金時代。北方則誕生了抵抗政權：七一八年北逃的佩拉約在阿斯圖里亞斯立足，七二二年科瓦東加之役被記為伊比利亞基督教抵抗的起點，此後萊昂、卡斯提爾、阿拉貢、納瓦拉相繼形成，最終引出長達八百年的收復失地運動；七七八年法蘭克查理曼在龍塞斯瓦列斯敗於巴斯克與阿拉伯聯軍，說明新秩序並非無往不利。阿拉伯語與伊斯蘭在安達盧斯扎下根，安達盧斯的科學、醫學與數學知識，後來又經西西里與地中海航路傳回歐洲。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reach far beyond Iberia. In the short term, the Visigothic kingdom that had endured for close to three centuries since 418 collapsed within a single year: the king was killed, the capital fell, the bishops and nobles of Toledo accepted conversion and kept their churches and their landed arrangements, and the Mozarabic Christian communities continued in al-Andalus for centuries, later forming a bridge to the Christian world north of the Pyrenees. Muslim al-Andalus was thereby founded on the Iberian peninsula, governed for its first eighty years directly from the caliphate in Damascus, until in 756 the Umayyad prince Abd al-Rahman I crossed the sea from Syria to Cordoba and founded an independent emirate with Cordoba as its capital, opening three centuries often called the golden age of al-Andalus. To the north the resisting polities were born: Pelayo, who had fled north in 718, established himself in Asturias, and the battle of Covadonga in 722 is recorded as the starting point of Christian resistance in Iberia, after which Leon, Castile, Aragon and Navarre took shape and the long Reconquista followed; in 778 Charlemagne was defeated at Roncesvalles by a coalition of Basques and Arabs, showing that the new order was not invincible. Arabic and Islam took root in al-Andalus, and the science, medicine and mathematics of al-Andalus later travelled back into Europe through Sicily and the Mediterranean sea routes.
result: 結果是安達盧斯的易手與倭馬亞秩序的建立，但並非一次完成。瓜達萊特一役決定了西哥特王室的命運：七一一年七月，王軍在瓜達萊特河畔被擊潰，羅德里克陣亡，西哥特人退回托勒多，城中教會與貴族選擇有條件的歸降——主教奧勒留斯與法爾加里烏斯等人在托勒多的清真寺接受哈里發代表，換取教會存續與社團自治。八月十日穆薩進入托勒多，隨後是薩拉戈薩、托爾托薩、穆爾西亞，七一八年優素福·菲赫里的鎮壓使安達盧斯的主要城市都落在穆斯林統治之下，倭馬亞朝在北非與安達盧斯的關係也從此固定下來。遠征軍自身的結局卻是分裂的：塔里克沒有看到西班牙全境落入手中，七一五年後他被召回北非，死在推羅附近；穆薩及其子後來在安達盧斯與突尼斯都陷入爭鬥，七四四年伊本·庫萊德率軍將穆薩家族掃出安達盧斯；留下來的倭馬亞王朝，要到七五六年才由阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼一世重建。回頭看，這場戰爭的勝利是用一場會戰、一紙協議和一代人的順勢推進換來的，而它的長期代價則由北方的基督徒王國用近八百年時間償還。
resultEn: The result was the transfer of al-Andalus and the establishment of Umayyad order, but it was not accomplished in a single stroke. The battle of Guadalete settled the fate of the Visigothic royal house: in July 711 the royal army was destroyed on the banks of the Guadalete, Roderic was killed, and the Visigoths fell back into Toledo, where the church and the nobility chose a conditional submission, the bishops Aurelius and Fulgarius receiving the representative of the caliph in the mosque at Toledo in exchange for the survival of the church and for communal autonomy. Musa entered Toledo on 10 August, followed by Zaragoza, Tortosa and Murcia, and the suppression carried out by Yusuf al-Fihri in 718 placed all the major cities of al-Andalus under Muslim rule, settling the relationship between the Umayyad house in North Africa and al-Andalus for good. The expedition's own ending was a division: Tariq never saw the whole of Spain fall into his hands and was recalled to North Africa after 715, dying near Tripoli; Musa and his son afterwards fell into quarrels in al-Andalus and in Tunis alike, and in 744 Ibn Khaydad led the troops that swept the house of Musa out of al-Andalus; the Umayyad dynasty that remained had to wait until 756 to be rebuilt by Abd al-Rahman I. Looking back, the victory in this war was bought with a single battle, a written agreement and a generation of momentum, while its long bill was paid by the Christian kingdoms of the north over close to eight centuries.
